title: Financial Returns
body:
A **return** is the fractional change in price over a period, and every statistic in the
project is computed on returns.

```
simple return:   r = (P_end - P_start) / P_start

100 -> 110       r = 10/100 = 0.10, or 10%
```

Prices are the wrong input for three reasons. They are not comparable across assets, since a
$10 move is large at $20 and negligible at $2000. They trend, so the mean and standard
deviation of a price series describe the trend, and the variation around it is what the risk
measures need. And they have units, so no statistic computed on them compares between stocks.

A return series fixes all three. It is dimensionless, roughly stationary, and directly
comparable, which is what makes the mean and [[Variance]] from [[STATISTICS]] meaningful when
applied to it.

**Log returns**, $\ln(P_{end}/P_{start})$, are the alternative. They add across periods, so a
sequence of them sums to the total, where simple returns compound and have to be multiplied.
For the 10% move above the log return is 0.0953, and the two agree closely for small moves and
diverge for large ones.

[[Volatility]] and the [[Sharpe Ratio]] are both computed from this series.
